## Observed Facts
Data Scope: BGL, whole period (2005-06-03 15:42:50 to 2006-01-04 08:00:05 [E1]), level = FATAL, no other filters. There are 855,195 FATAL Log Entries in total [E2]. They come from four Components [E2]:

| Component | FATAL Log Entries |
|---|---|
| KERNEL | 626,450 [E2] |
| APP | 228,536 [E2] |
| LINKCARD | 206 [E2] |
| MMCS | 3 [E2] |

KERNEL and APP together account for nearly all FATAL Log Entries. These are Log Entry counts, not incidents.

## Hypotheses
- Repeated messages could be inflating the KERNEL and APP counts. A single fault can be logged many times, so these counts may reflect a small number of distinct problems. I haven't checked this.
- LINKCARD and MMCS have very few FATAL Log Entries. They may be rare but important hardware or control-system events. This is also unchecked.

## Unknowns
- I haven't looked at how the FATAL counts are spread over time. I don't know whether they are steady, recurring or concentrated in a few bursts.
- I haven't looked at the message content. I don't know which distinct problems sit behind the KERNEL and APP counts.
- I haven't looked at which nodes are involved.

## Next Step
1. Run a daily or weekly trend of FATAL Log Entries for KERNEL and APP, to see whether they recur or come in spikes.
2. Search or group the FATAL KERNEL messages to find the dominant problems. They make up about 73% of FATAL Log Entries (626,450 of 855,195 [E2]).
